question: Choose the figure that is different from the others (odd man out).
options: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100"><rect width="100" height="100" fill="#fff"/><polyline points="17,25.7 50.6,74.3 83,25.7" fill="none" stroke="#111" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-linejoin="round"/></svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100"><rect width="100" height="100" fill="#fff"/><polyline points="16.6,73.3 51.1,25.9 83.4,74.1" fill="none" stroke="#111" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-linejoin="round"/></svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100"><rect width="100" height="100" fill="#fff"/><polyline points="8,35.6 58.8,8 92,92" fill="none" stroke="#111" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-linejoin="round"/></svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100"><rect width="100" height="100" fill="#fff"/><polyline points="26.3,17.3 73.7,49.6 26.3,82.7" fill="none" stroke="#111" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-linejoin="round"/></svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100"><rect width="100" height="100" fill="#fff"/><polyline points="72.4,16.6 26.3,50.2 73.7,83.4" fill="none" stroke="#111" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-linejoin="round"/></svg>
why: Each figure is an angle made of two straight arms. In options 1, 2, 4 and 5 the two arms are equal in length; the angle is only turned to face different ways. In option 3 one arm is much longer than the other.
trick: Turning a figure does not make it different; compare the lengths of the parts instead.
